label: input token in {z,j,y,h,f,p}, from step 5 on
explanation: Input-token detector for a small set of letters, ranked z (40% active rate when input, 8x lift) > j > y > h > f > p. These six tokens carry about 89% of activation mass. It fires whether the token arrives as an original input or is fed back during the copy phase. In the copy phase it fires most at recall_idx 1-2, i.e. when the fed-back token is orig(0) or orig(1), and the top activations are a leading z echoed right after <DEL>. It is suppressed early in the sequence: almost never active at t<=3, and its rate rises with t and with L. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire more often than first occurrences. It is essentially silent at t=0 and on the <DEL> step. Precision is limited: even with t>=5, only about 35% of z/j/y/h/f/p inputs are active, and no history variable (prev/next tokens, first_tok) cleanly separates the active ones from the rest. Restricting to {z,j,y} or to the copy phase increases precision but loses mass.
